assessment_summary: 1. For tours C and D, write d(C,D)=|E(C)\E(D)|, the number of C-edges replaced. Thus D is reachable by a k-change exactly when d(C,D)≤k. 2. The half-exchange lemma for undirected Hamilton cycles states that, for fixed C, every tour-difference vector χ_D−χ_C is a nonnegative combination of vectors χ_Q−χ_C for tours Q satisfying d(C,Q)≤ceil(n/2). This follows by decomposing the symmetric difference into alternating exchanges and repeatedly splitting any exchange using more than half of C at consecutive removed C-edges; the two possible reconnections give smaller tour exchanges, and iteration terminates. 3. If C is ceil(n/2)-Opt locally optimal, then w·(χ_Q−χ_C)≥0 for every such Q. Applying this inequality to the nonnegative decomposition gives w·(χ_D−χ_C)≥0 for every tour D. Hence no tour is shorter than C, so C is globally optimal. The argument uses only additivity of edge weights; neither the triangle inequality nor strict positivity is needed.
